cards.front: What are the six essential nutrients?
cards.back: Carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water.

cards.front: What is the difference between macronutrients and micronutrients?
cards.back: Macronutrients are needed in large amounts (carbs, proteins, fats), while micronutrients are needed in small amounts (vitamins, minerals).

cards.front: What is the purpose of carbohydrates in the body?
cards.back: To provide energy, support brain function, and fuel physical activity.

cards.front: What are the different types of carbohydrates?
cards.back: Simple carbohydrates (sugars) and complex carbohydrates (starches and fiber).

cards.front: What is the importance of protein in nutrition?
cards.back: To build and repair tissues, support immune function, and provide energy.

cards.front: What are complete and incomplete proteins?
cards.back: Complete proteins contain all essential amino acids, while incomplete proteins lack one or more essential amino acids.

cards.front: What is the role of fats in the body?
cards.back: To provide energy, support cell function, and help absorb fat-soluble vitamins.

cards.front: What are the different types of fats?
cards.back: Saturated fats, unsaturated fats (monounsaturated and polyunsaturated), and trans fats.

cards.front: What is the importance of vitamins in nutrition?
cards.back: To support various body functions, prevent deficiencies, and maintain health.

cards.front: What are water-soluble and fat-soluble vitamins?
cards.back: Water-soluble vitamins (B and C) are not stored in the body, while fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) are stored in fat tissue.

cards.front: What is the purpose of minerals in the body?
cards.back: To support bone health, nerve function, and various metabolic processes.

cards.front: What are the major and trace minerals?
cards.back: Major minerals (calcium, phosphorus, magnesium) are needed in larger amounts, while trace minerals (iron, zinc, iodine) are needed in smaller amounts.

cards.front: What is the importance of water in nutrition?
cards.back: To maintain hydration, support digestion, and regulate body temperature.

cards.front: What is the purpose of dietary fiber?
cards.back: To support digestive health, regulate blood sugar, and promote satiety.

cards.front: What are the different types of dietary fiber?
cards.back: Soluble fiber (dissolves in water) and insoluble fiber (does not dissolve in water).

cards.front: What is the importance of meal planning?
cards.back: To ensure balanced nutrition, save time, and control food costs.

cards.front: What are the benefits of food preservation?
cards.back: To extend shelf life, maintain nutritional value, and prevent food waste.

cards.front: What is the purpose of food safety practices?
cards.back: To prevent foodborne illnesses and ensure safe food consumption.

cards.front: What are the key principles of food safety?
cards.back: Clean, separate, cook, and chill.

cards.front: What is the importance of food labeling?
cards.back: To provide nutritional information, ingredient lists, and allergen warnings.

cards.front: What are the benefits of organic foods?
cards.back: Reduced pesticide exposure, potential environmental benefits, and often better taste.

cards.front: What is the purpose of food fortification?
cards.back: To add essential nutrients to foods and prevent deficiencies.

cards.front: What are the different types of cooking methods?
cards.back: Dry heat methods (baking, grilling) and moist heat methods (boiling, steaming).

cards.front: What is the importance of food storage?
cards.back: To maintain quality, prevent spoilage, and ensure food safety.

cards.front: What are the benefits of meal prep?
cards.back: Time savings, portion control, and better nutrition planning.

cards.front: What is the purpose of nutritional assessment?
cards.back: To evaluate dietary intake, identify deficiencies, and plan interventions.

cards.front: What are the different types of diets?
cards.back: Mediterranean, vegetarian, vegan, ketogenic, and balanced diets.

cards.front: What is the importance of portion control?
cards.back: To manage calorie intake, maintain healthy weight, and prevent overeating.

cards.front: What are the benefits of mindful eating?
cards.back: Better digestion, improved satisfaction, and healthier relationship with food.

cards.front: What is the purpose of food allergies and intolerances management?
cards.back: To prevent adverse reactions and ensure safe food consumption.

cards.front: What are the key factors in choosing healthy foods?
cards.back: Nutritional value, freshness, processing level, and personal preferences.

cards.front: What is the importance of food sustainability?
cards.back: To protect the environment, support local communities, and ensure future food security.

cards.front: What are the benefits of seasonal eating?
cards.back: Better taste, higher nutritional value, and environmental benefits.

cards.front: What is the purpose of food waste reduction?
cards.back: To save money, protect the environment, and improve food security.

cards.front: What are the different types of food processing?
cards.back: Minimal processing, moderate processing, and ultra-processing.

cards.front: What is the importance of food education?
cards.back: To promote healthy eating habits and improve nutritional knowledge.

cards.front: What are the benefits of home cooking?
cards.back: Better control over ingredients, cost savings, and improved nutrition.

cards.front: What is the purpose of food budgeting?
cards.back: To manage food costs, plan purchases, and reduce waste.

cards.front: What are the key elements of a balanced diet?
cards.back: Variety, moderation, and appropriate portion sizes.

cards.front: What is the importance of food culture?
cards.back: To preserve traditions, promote diversity, and enhance social connections.

cards.front: What are the benefits of food innovation?
cards.back: Improved nutrition, better taste, and enhanced convenience.

cards.front: What is the purpose of food research?
cards.back: To improve nutrition, develop new products, and enhance food safety.

cards.front: What are the different types of food careers?
cards.back: Nutritionist, chef, food scientist, and dietitian.

cards.front: What is the importance of food ethics?
cards.back: To ensure fair practices, animal welfare, and environmental responsibility.

cards.front: What are the key factors in food success?
cards.back: Quality, nutrition, taste, and sustainability.

cards.front: What is the purpose of food marketing?
cards.back: To promote products, educate consumers, and influence purchasing decisions.

cards.front: What are the benefits of food collaboration?
cards.back: Knowledge sharing, innovation, and improved outcomes.

cards.front: What is the importance of food accessibility?
cards.back: To ensure all people have access to nutritious and affordable food.

cards.front: What are the different types of food systems?
cards.back: Local, regional, national, and global food systems.

cards.front: What is the purpose of food policy?
cards.back: To regulate food production, ensure safety, and promote public health.

cards.front: What are the key elements of food excellence?
cards.back: Quality, nutrition, safety, and sustainability.
